transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-03
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Sofia Ramos (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood Product), Ethan Cole (Nimbus ML Platform), Priya Nair (CTO), Arjun Mehta (SRE), Leah Ortiz (PM)

Summary (auto-gen, may be brief):
Quick model catalog demo focusing on selecting open models, understanding the compatibility matrix across GPUs and quantization profiles, and where Redwood Optimize suggests batching/caching knobs. Action items: share compatibility CSV and benchmark XLS, schedule sizing session, provide security docs.

--- Transcript ---
00:00 Jamie Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, Ethan, Priya, Arjun, Leah — appreciate you squeezing this in. I'm Jamie from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Sofia, Liam, you want to quick intros?
00:07 Sofia Ramos: Yeah hi all, Sofia, I'm a solutions engineer, I'll run through the model catalog and compatibility matrix and then show a couple perf profiles in the console. Sorry if my audio is a bit low, I moved rooms.
00:13 Ethan Cole: No problem. Quick note, we're recording this internally but happy to keep your recording too. We're focused on inference cost and tail latency — 200 ms 95p is our target for chat flows, sometimes 100 ms for critical paths.
00:26 Jamie Park: Great — that's helpful. Today's agenda: short catalog walkthrough, compatibility matrix, benchmark signals, then Optimize recommendations and Q&A. We'll leave time at the end for next steps.
00:35 Priya Nair: Sounds good. Also want to confirm we're able to evaluate private deployments — we have a compliance window for end of November.
00:42 Sofia Ramos: Absolutely, we'll point out Dedicated and Private options as we go and notes about KMS and SAML.
00:48 01:10 Sofia Ramos: (screen-share) Alright opening the Console — top left is the Model Catalog. Quick note: catalog shows curated open models plus Redwood-verified performance profiles. You can filter by task, e.g., chat, summarization, embeddings, and by tokenization behavior.
01:30 Sofia Ramos: For Nimbus's chat use-case, I usually start filtering by 'chat' and then 'context length >= 8k' because you mentioned long histories. See here, the compatibility matrix icon — click that.
01:44 Arjun Mehta: That icon — does it reflect exact kernel-level support per GPU?
01:48 Sofia Ramos: It maps compatibility at the runtime level: architecture support, recommended quantization profiles (e.g., 4-bit, 8-bit), and whether KV cache optimizations are enabled. It's an opinionated mapping from our runtime tests — sometimes the kernel name is inaccurate in the UI, like it says 'cuda-kernal-9' in some older rows, a transcribe quirk.
02:03 Leah Ortiz: Can you export that? We want to push into our internal tool.
02:06 Sofia Ramos: Yes, export CSV or JSON. We'll include the matrix in the follow-up.
02:12 03:00 Sofia Ramos: (narrating) Here is a candidate shortlist: Llama-3-8k, Mistral-7B-v2, RedPine-13B-open, and a 7B distilled variant. Mistral shows very good throughput on A100s in our tests, but Llama variants have better generation quality on some instruction sets. Note: transcription sometimes shows 'Redpine' as 'Red-pine' or 'red flim' — ignore that.
03:33 Ethan Cole: For our production load, we run batch and real-time. What do you recommend for routing? Dedicated pool for real-time and hosted for batch?
03:40 Jamie Park: That's a common pattern. You can pin high-SLA routes to Dedicated and use hosted to overflow for non-sensitive data. Also routing policies can fallback to quantized variants if the primary model is unavailable.
03:58 Sofia Ramos: (screen) Now jumping into the benchmark tab — we demo a 'perf profile' for Mistral-7B-v2 on an A10G vs a T4. The numbers are median throughput and p95 token latency for a 512 token completion. For A10G we saw ~1200 tok/s and 95p latency around 210ms when uncached; on T4 it's lower — and note the run configs: batch size = 4, KV cache warm.
04:32 Priya Nair: Those numbers seem higher than our internal runs on colab GPUs; can you clarify quantization?
04:36 Sofia Ramos: Sure. The table shows three rows per model: float16 full, 8-bit quant, and awq/4-bit. Our runtime labels 4-bit as 'int4-approx' sometimes in logs. AWQ reduces memory and can improve throughput on Ampere, but may increase per-token variance.
04:50 Arjun Mehta: Any empirical regressions on hallucination when using 4-bit awq?
04:53 Sofia Ramos: For most instruction-tuning workloads we didn't see systematic regressions, but we recommend running the Redwood Optimize eval set — you can tie your prompt set to the quality monitors. We'll export the eval run in the follow-up.
05:10 06:05 Sofia Ramos: (shows compatibility matrix export dialog) This CSV includes columns: model, arch, recommended_quant, kernel_notes, example_throughput_med, example_p95_latency. There's also a hardware-compatibility flag: vram_min_gb and preferred_gpu_family.
06:30 Ethan Cole: If we pick RedPine-13B-open for a pilot, what's the minimal VRAM? We have some 48GB A40s and a few 80GB A100s.
06:38 Sofia Ramos: RedPine-13B-open with 8-bit runs on 48GB with 8-bit quant and reduced max seq length. For best latency use 80GB. We'll include exact recommended configs per model in the CSV.
06:50 Liam O'Connor: Also call out that Dedicated pools can be configured with pinning to specific GPU families so you don't mix A40 with A100 if you want consistent latency.
07:02 Priya Nair: Regarding network security for Private - we require SAML SSO and customer-managed KMS. Is that supported?
07:08 Jamie Park: Yes — Private supports SAML, Enterprise SSO, and KMS/HSM integrations. We also provide audit logs and optional WORM retention for compliance-heavy customers.
07:20 Ethan Cole: Is audit logging exported to their SIEM?
07:23 Sofia Ramos: Yes, log forwarding to Splunk or Datadog is supported, and you can push logs via our private collector for on-prem. Occasionally the service name is mis-transcribed as 'Redwood logs shipper' as 'redwood bog shipper' in our exports.
07:33 09:10 Sofia Ramos: (demonstration) Now Optimize tab — the system suggests batching and cache policies based on your observed token distribution. For example, for our sample chat traces, Optimize suggests batch window 25ms, micro-batch size 8 on A100, and prefix caching for stable system prompts. These are heuristics driven by cost-models.
09:45 Leah Ortiz: Can Optimize surface cost delta if we change quantization?
09:48 Sofia Ramos: Yes, in the UI it shows estimated cost per 1M tokens for each config variant and projected latency. We also export a cost-comparison CSV so you can plug into your financial model.
10:05 Arjun Mehta: Curious about routing policies in multi-model setups — if primary model is overburdened will the runtime restart the request on a quantized variant? That adds latency.
10:11 Jamie Park: The runtime can stream a quick decision: fallback to a compatible model that's pinned for a route, or shift to hosted if Dedicated capacity is exhausted. Fallbacks are configurable — immediate fallback vs queued retry. We recommend canary thresholds to avoid surprise regressions.
10:30 12:00 Sofia Ramos: (note on transcription) We're seeing occasional mislabeling of the kernel tests — e.g., 'faster-nsv kernel' is actually 'faster-ns v2' — but numbers are reliable.
12:18 Ethan Cole: For our SLO we want 200ms p95 with 95% of requests under that. Do you have sample configurations?
12:25 Sofia Ramos: Yes — for 200ms p95 you typically need A100 or A10G with warm KV cache and batch sizes small (1-4). We'll send two recommended configs: one cost-optimized (8-bit on A10G) and one latency-optimized (fp16 on A100).
12:40 Priya Nair: Will using dedicated pools affect our data residency? We need logs and telemetry to remain inside our VPC.
12:46 Jamie Park: Private deployments keep telemetry in your VPC; Dedicated still routes telemetry to Redwood's control plane unless you opt for Private with the collector. We'll include a matrix of data flow in the security doc.
13:05 15:00 Sofia Ramos: (narration) Switching to a quick live run — I'm going to run a tiny benchmark for Mistral-7B-v2, 512 tokens, batch=2. Starting run...
15:18 Sofia Ramos: Hmm looks like the first run is high latency — 1st token cold startup. I'm re-running to warm the KV cahce... (typo on screen).
15:45 Sofia Ramos: Second run results: median tok/s 1140, p95 token latency 230ms on our A10G cluster. CPU/IO time is negligible; most variance from kernel dispatch and memory swaps.
16:05 Ethan Cole: Can we request raw perf logs for these runs?
16:09 Sofia Ramos: Yes we can attach run artifacts — includes perf counters, GPU utilization, and mem maps. We'll redact any internal node hostnames before sharing.
16:20 18:00 Jamie Park: Quick question on procurement: what does Nimbus typically need to sign for Dedicated trials?
18:05 Priya Nair: We need 60-day trial terms, NDAs already signed, plus terms about data retention. Our legal team will ask for SOC2 report and subprocessor list.
18:16 Jamie Park: Great — we'll include SOC2 and subproc. Also we'll share the dedicated trial doc outlining expected commit levels.
18:28 20:00 Sofia Ramos: Back to compatibility — there are edge cases where a model uses fused ops that our runtime hasn't optimized for on certain GPU kernels. We flag those in the matrix as 'partial-optim' and include recommended fallbacks.
20:35 Arjun Mehta: Any known issues with Mistral-7B-v2 and 4-bit AWQ on older drivers?
20:40 Sofia Ramos: Yes driver versions < 530 can cause kernel fallback; we note minimum driver in the CSV. Sometimes transcriptions show 'five-thirty' as 'fifty-thirty' so check the value.
20:55 Liam O'Connor: Also remember model family heuristics — some Llama forks have different tokenizer behavior that effects token counts. We provide tokenization deltas in the catalog.
21:12 Leah Ortiz: Can we ask Redwood to run our exact prompt suite through these models?
21:16 Jamie Park: Absolutely — action item for Sofia to run the three prompt sets you share and return latency and a basic quality diff.
21:26 Ethan Cole: We'll upload the prompt sets to the shared S3 link you provided during POC intake.
21:31 Sofia Ramos: Great — I'll kick off evals as soon as we have the sets. Expect a CSV with per-prompt latency, tokens, and an optional rouge/bleu-like automated metric for structured outputs.
21:45 24:00 Sofia Ramos: (shows an example of routing policy editor) You can define route priorities, weight splits, and a fallback model. You can also set per-route SLOs which triggers automatic traffic shift if a p95 breach happens.
24:28 Priya Nair: What observability does Redwood provide on per-token billing spikes?
24:32 Jamie Park: Token-level cost breakdowns, and you can set cost alerts. We also expose tokenization deltas per prompt so you can estimate spikes.
24:55 Ethan Cole: About the benchmark CSV — does it include synthetic tests or real-workload traces?
25:00 Sofia Ramos: Both. We include synthetic microbenchmarks (cold/warm KV cache, various batch sizes) and a couple of representative real traces from our internal benchmark corpus. We'll note which rows are synthetic.
25:20 28:00 Sofia Ramos: (small digression) Quick callout on model licensing for 'RedPine' — some open variants have restrictive terms; our catalog flags license types. If you need to run in Private with stricter licensing we can advise.
28:30 Priya Nair: We care about model provenance and the PII risk in training data. Any tooling for PII detection in outputs?
28:36 Sofia Ramos: We have output filters and a redaction pipeline as part of Private deployments; also you can add a post-processing function via function-calls to scrub PII. We'll include docs.
28:54 30:00 Jamie Park: Timecheck — about 20 minutes left. Want to make sure we cover next steps and scheduling the Dedicated sizing session.
30:12 Priya Nair: Yes let's pick a day next week for infra folks.
30:16 Jamie Park: How's 2025-10-08 for a 60-minute deep-dive with Arjun and our infra team?
30:21 Arjun Mehta: Works.
30:23 Jamie Park: Perfect.
30:30 32:00 Sofia Ramos: (final demo point) One last thing — the Optimize runbook can generate a suggested rollout: start hosted smoke, run a small dedicated pool for canary, then shift 30% traffic for 48 hours if metrics are green. It's a codified rollout you can copy as a YAML. Sometimes transcription shows 'YAML' as 'yammel' in the notes.
32:45 Leah Ortiz: Would the canary include a quality gate?
32:48 Sofia Ramos: Yes, the gate can be tied to your eval set; we compute a regression score and block traffic shift if it drops below threshold.
33:05 Ethan Cole: Two quick asks: 1) full compatibility CSV, 2) sample perf runs with raw logs, 3) pricing scenarios for Dedicated pilot.
33:15 Jamie Park: Noted — we'll deliver all three.
33:20 Jamie Park: Any remaining questions on models or compat?
33:23 Priya Nair: No more from me.
33:25 Arjun Mehta: One more: can we pin model versions for rollout? We need reproducible inference.
33:30 Sofia Ramos: Yes you can pin and freeze versions, and Redwood supports immutable model artifacts in Private.
33:40 Jamie Park: Alright wrapping up — recap and next steps: we'll send compatibility CSV, benchmark XLS with run artifacts, SOC2 + SAML docs, and Dedicated trial terms. Schedule: deep-dive on 2025-10-08. Action items sent in chat.
33:58 Ethan Cole: Thanks everyone.
34:02 Priya Nair: Thanks, really helpful.
34:10 Jamie Park: Thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invite and the artifacts.
34:20 (call ends)

Notes about transcript quality: automated transcription sometimes merged speaker lines and mistranscribed technical phrases (e.g., 'KV cahce' instead of 'KV cache', 'kernel' as 'kernal'). We preserved filler words and short crosstalk.

References shared during call:
- Model compatibility export (CSV) - will be attached to follow-up
- Benchmark artifacts ZIP - run logs + perf counters
- Security pack (SOC2, SAML, KMS integration doc)
- Shared S3 link for prompt sets (provided in chat)

End of transcript.
